input.quote: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment. In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.6, then, in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay to SFJ within [***] of the date of termination an amount equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of Development Costs which were paid or incurred by SFJ.
input.rationale: The assignment clause itself (§ 15.6, p0814) is acceptable: it is mutual, requires consent only for other transfers, and expressly carves out assignment to Affiliates or to a successor in a merger, stock sale or sale of substantially all assets (including by operation of law), which meets the preferred position on Customer assignment (the Affiliate/successor guarantee mechanics in p0816 are mutual and not a material issue). The deviation is § 14.2.6 (p0765): a Change of Control of PB — defined broadly at p0036–p0037 to include a 50% voting-power change or sale of the Product business — gives SFJ a sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement and accelerates a payment of 150% of Development Costs against PB. That is exactly the walk-away case under this rule (a counterparty right to terminate or re-price on our change of control) and it is not cured by PB's optional Change of Control Buy-Out under § 6.7.2 (p0530), which is a separate PB election. We therefore delete SFJ's change-of-control termination right and the related 150% payment, keeping PB's notice obligation and its continuing development and Approval Payment obligations (p0766) intact.

proposal.summary: Delete SFJ's right to terminate on a Change of Control of PB (and the related 150% payment), retaining PB's notice obligation and post-closing performance covenants.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted SFJ's discretionary right to terminate (and the associated 150% of Development Costs payment) on a Change of Control of PB: our playbook does not permit a counterparty exit or re-pricing triggered by our change of control. PB's notice obligation and its continuing development and Approval Payment obligations (including SFJ's buy-out economics under Section 6.7.2) are unchanged.
